whl_sexton.text: Rob Roy lies in the kirkyard outside, with his wife Mary and two of his sons. The stone has a sword on it and a Celtic cross, and a surprising number of visitors lay coins on it.

He was nearly sixty-three when he died, which for a man who'd been hunted most of his life is a good innings. The story says he received his last visitors fully dressed, with his sword and his bagpipes.
He asked for the pipes to be played as he died. Whether it's true or not, nobody dared contradict a MacGregor. Not at the time.
